newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says ready to scrap Rwanda arms deal.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says ready to scrap Rwanda arms deal.

text.p: South Africa said on Monday it would cancel its 87 million rand ($18.5 million) arms deal with Rwanda if asked to do so by leaders at an African summit on Tuesday dealing with the conflict in eastern Zaire.

Cabinet minister Kader Asmal, chairman of the National Conventional Arms Control Committee that decides on Pretoria's arms exports, said South Africa would be guided by leaders of the Great Lakes states surrounding Rwanda and Zaire.
"We will follow the advice of the Great Lakes region," Asmal told reporters.

He said his committee was scheduled to meet on November 14, but that he and Defence Minister Joe Modise could cancel or suspend the contract if this was deemed to be in South Africa's national interest.
Asmal said South Africa had so far delivered armoured personnel carriers to Rwanda. His government has declined to reveal details of the contract which is also believed to include small arms.

East and Central African leaders are scheduled to meet in Nairobi on Tuesday to discuss the worsening situation in eastern Zaire, where ethnic Tutsi rebels, with the support of the Rwandan army, have been battling Zairean government troops.
South Africa has come in for criticism for its September decision to lift a ban on arms sales to Rwanda.

Human rights observers say the Great Lakes region is awash with weapons from various countries including Belgium, China, Chile, Egypt, France, Germany, Israel, Romania, Russia, South Africa, the United States and Yugoslavia.
Rivalry between majority Hutus and minority ethnic Tutsis has troubled Rwanda and Burundi for generations and has now spilled on to the territory of mineral-rich Zaire.
Foreign armies have denied fighting alongside Tutsi rebels in Zaire but Rwanda has said it sent troops on an incursion this week after artillery and machinegun exchanges across its border.
Around one million ethnic Hutu refugees in war-torn eastern Zaire have been on the move as fighting between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops raged.
